anomalies.observed: The schematic contains an additional resistor R16 with value 1k connected from the TTL/serial servo-bus node to GND. This resistor is not listed in the specification's component table or bias-network description.
anomalies.expected: The specified design uses R13/R14 0 ohm jumpers to connect J3/J8 pin 3 to the shared TTL bus, and the MAX3485 bias/pull network is described as R6, R8, and R15 (2k, 2.2k, 2.2k). There is no specified 1k pull-down resistor on the TTL/serial-bus node.

evidence.quote: R16 1k connected to GND near the TTL label (sheet m5-pantilt.kicad_sch, page 1/1)
R6, R7, R8, R15 | 2k, 20k, 2.2k, 2.2k | Bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line.
R13, R14 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus

anomalies.impact: The extra 1k pull-down lowers the impedance of the shared serial/TTL bus and changes the intended fail-safe biasing. In serial servo mode this can corrupt the idle level or load the MAX3485 driver, potentially preventing reliable half-duplex communication.

parsed.summary: Most of the schematic matches the specified stack-chan pan-tilt design, but it includes an undocumented 1k pull-down resistor R16 on the TTL/serial servo-bus node, which is a deviation from the intended bias and jumpering scheme.
